title: Pancreatic stone protein (PSP) for the early detection of sepsis in severe burns
summary:
Burn victims are at high risk of infection, such as sepsis, due to their wounds. Sepsis is a life-threatening complication. Early detection and timely initiation of treatment are crucial for improving the success of the therapy. Established blood tests can indicate sepsis. However, these often have limitations, such as a delayed response and insufficient sensitivity in the early detection of sepsis in burn victims.
Pancreatic stone protein (PSP) has proven to be a promising blood parameter for the early detection of sepsis. Studies have shown that PSP levels rise significantly even before visible symptoms of sepsis appear. This would allow for very early diagnosis and treatment. Using a special device (abioSCOPE), PSP can be easily measured from the patient's blood directly in the burn unit. The blood does not need to be sent to a laboratory for this test. The result is available within minutes and can improve bedside decision-making regarding infection control measures.
The aim of this pilot study is to investigate the feasibility, accuracy, and clinical utility of the PSP test using the abioSCOPE device in severely burned adults.
conditions: Burns of multiple regions, unspecified degree

interventions.name: From routine morning blood draws on days 0–20, 50 µl are taken each time and analyzed using abioSCOPE. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients ≥ 18 years
Burns > 15% of total body surface area, 2nd-3rd degree
Exclusion criteria:
Lack of consent to study participation
Hospital admission > 24 hours after burn injury
Primarily palliative therapy
Known acute or chronic pancreatitis or pancreatic cancer
